answer: The strongest sybil resistance comes from making identity expensive to manufacture: each agent must post a stake and accumulate a verifiable record of unique, attested work before it may transact. A ferrous anchorage driven through canyon bedrock is the right analogy, because every claimed identity is pinned to a costly, traceable history, and karst-like clusters of shared infrastructure are cross-checked and collapsed. Spawning thousands of fake agents then means paying real compute and risking slashed stake, which normally exceeds any reward.
